language.script_notes: Spanish as the primary official/signage language nationwide; Quechua and Aymara are co-official and spoken widely in the Andean highlands, occasionally appearing on cultural/tourism signage.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Slim, 'cigarette-shaped' bollards, often white with yellow stripes — rarely seen outside Peru, making this a strong national tell.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Slim cylindrical post, sometimes with black stripes; also triangular-shaped concrete bollards.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Black-and-yellow diagonally striped guardrails on sharp curves — Peru's stripe uses a black outer edge, distinguishing it from Bolivia's similar-looking yellow-outer-edge striping.
road_furniture.line_paint: White outside/white inside or white outside/yellow inside lines.
road_furniture.curb_style: Orange-and-black diagonal stripes also appear on curbs at sharp curves. Lima features long, straight boulevard-style streets divided by a concrete or grassy median, unusual within Peru.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Distinctive black-and-white striped sign poles with a concrete block base are one of the best Peru-specific visual tells in South America. Repsol, Primax, PetroPeru and Pecsa are common fuel-station brands.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs common on unfinished/informal concrete buildings nationwide (rebar often left exposed for future additions); red-tile pitched roofs in colonial-era highland towns.
architecture.roof_material: Flat poured concrete widespread; red clay tile in colonial Andean towns like Cusco.
architecture.wall_construction: Highly regional — see Coast/Andean Highlands/Amazon profiles for specifics; unfinished exposed-brick and rebar construction extremely common nationwide as a general Peru/Andean-region tell.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Varies by region; unpainted brick/concrete is common nationwide alongside occasional brightly painted buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Spanish colonial architecture built atop Inca stone foundations in the highlands; unfinished multi-story concrete/brick buildings nationwide; ancient Inca sites (Machu Picchu, Sacsayhuamán) as unique landmarks.

nature.vegetation: Three starkly different zones — a narrow, mostly barren coastal desert; high Andean grassland (puna) and cloud forest in the highlands; dense equatorial Amazon rainforest to the east. See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: The Andes run the length of the country, dividing the arid Pacific coastal strip from the Amazon basin to the east — Peru contains some of the world's highest mountains alongside vast lowland rainforest.
nature.climate_signature: Extremely varied by region — desert coast, cold high-altitude Andes, hot humid Amazon — regional identification is essential in Peru.

vehicles.plate_color: White plates for private vehicles, yellow for commercial/taxi.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Tuktuks (three-wheeled auto rickshaws) are common in Peru and essentially absent from the rest of Latin America — a near-unique, highly reliable Peru tell.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed Gen 3/4 official coverage supplemented by Trekker imagery in the Amazon and remote highlands.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring; some coverage sourced from unofficial/third-party cameras in remote areas.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense around Lima and major highland cities; sparse and patchy in the Amazon basin.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andean altiplano terrain and Quechua/Aymara cultural presence, similar striped guardrails on mountain roads
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's guardrail stripe has a black outer edge vs. Bolivia's yellow outer edge; Peru's tuktuks are common while Bolivia has few; Bolivia is landlocked while Peru has a long Pacific coastline.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andean highland terrain and some Amazon rainforest overlap to the east
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's black-and-white striped sign poles with concrete bases and cigarette-shaped bollards are distinctive versus Ecuador's road furniture; plate formats also differ.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Atacama-adjacent coastal desert stretching across the shared border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peruvian road furniture (striped poles, cigarette bollards) differs from Chile's yellow-reflector bollards; Peru shows more visible Andean/Quechua cultural presence than northern Chile.
